## New resources

Five resources that make access control and guardrails manageable from configuration:

- `ona_group` — custom organization groups. Groups are the subject of every access grant, so this is the anchor the two policy resources depend on.
- `ona_runner_policy` — grants a group `RUNNER_ROLE_ADMIN` or `RUNNER_ROLE_USER` on a runner. Runners created by Terraform were admin-only until now.
- `ona_project_policy` — grants a group `PROJECT_ROLE_ADMIN`, `PROJECT_ROLE_EDITOR` or `PROJECT_ROLE_USER` on a project. Members also need access to a runner the project uses before they can start environments.
- `ona_service_account` — the non-human identity automation authenticates as. Tokens are not managed here; create them in the Ona UI or through the API.
- `ona_security_policy` — port and executable guardrails for environments the policy is assigned to.

```hcl
resource "ona_group" "platform" {
  name        = "platform"
  description = "Platform engineering team"
}

resource "ona_runner_policy" "platform_admin" {
  runner_id = ona_runner.example.id
  group_id  = ona_group.platform.id
  role      = "RUNNER_ROLE_ADMIN"
}
```

`ona_runner_policy` and `ona_project_policy` are keyed by a pair, so they import as `<runner-id>/<group-id>` and `<project-id>/<group-id>`. The other three import by ID.

## Changes

- Configuration is now validated during `terraform plan` instead of part-way through an apply. Enum attributes (`role`, `provider_type`, `variant`, `release_channel`, `log_level`, `target_mode`, executor `principal`, `max_admission_level`, rule `effect`), the UTC hour attributes, `max_retries`, and the `ona_project` initializer's `context_url`/`git` choice all report against the attribute in the configuration. Accepted enum names come from the SDK, so they cannot drift.
- Name and description lengths are checked against the limits the API enforces: `ona_group` name 3–80 and description ≤255, `ona_service_account` name 1–64 and description ≤500, `ona_runner` name 3–127, `ona_project` name 1–80. A configuration that exceeded these already failed at apply; it now fails at plan.
- `ona_service_account`'s `valid_until` is required, because the API requires an expiry, and immutable, so changing it replaces the account. Deleting a service account is a soft delete: a suspended account is treated as gone during refresh.
- `ona_security_policy` treats `executables.rules` as a set, since the API attaches no meaning to rule order, and exposes `default_effect` as read-only.
- System-managed groups and service accounts are rejected during refresh rather than mutated. Remove them from state with `terraform state rm`.
